title: Long-term contract with a loss year — Summit Builders
instructions: Summit Builders is constructing a distribution center on the customer's land for a fixed price of **$12,000,000**. Summit concludes revenue is recognized over time and measures progress with the **cost-to-cost** method. Enter losses as negative numbers.

exhibits.title: Contract data
exhibits.content:
| | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cumulative costs incurred | 3,000,000 | 7,200,000 | 12,400,000 |
| Estimated costs to complete | 6,000,000 | 5,300,000 | 0 |

parts.prompt: Compute the gross profit (loss) recognized each year.

rows.label: Year 2 gross profit (loss)
rows.explanation: Estimated total cost 12,500,000 > price → expected loss 500,000, recognized in full. Year 2 = −500,000 cumulative − 1,000,000 already recognized = **(1,500,000)**.

rows.label: Year 3 gross profit (loss)
rows.explanation: Actual total loss = 12,000,000 − 12,400,000 = (400,000). Cumulative recognized through Year 2 = (500,000). Year 3 = **+100,000**.

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) best supports recognizing Summit's revenue over time?

excerpts.text: If a performance obligation is not satisfied over time, the entity satisfies it at a point in time, considering indicators such as a present right to payment, legal title, physical possession, and customer acceptance.
An entity transfers control over time if its performance creates or enhances an asset (for example, work in process) that the customer controls as the asset is created or enhanced.
An entity estimates variable consideration using either the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever better predicts the consideration to which it will be entitled.
The incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer are recognized as an asset if the entity expects to recover them.

parts.explanation: The building is on the customer's land, so the customer controls the asset as it is constructed — the second over-time criterion.
